source_snapshot.criteria: System remains normal; BMC/UEFI may record a PCIe error; front-panel fault light may illuminate.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Does not prove PCIe AER severity, exact slot or post-UCE link/device recovery and uses generic MCE patterns.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly gates the UCE but leaves every management/indicator criterion optional and does not define which AER bit establishes non-fatal behavior.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Baseline row 33 is the OCP UCE variant and was not recounted; row 34 is eDPC/CTO with register-level DPC coverage.
historical_reviews.v3_1: A UCE label does not guarantee non-fatal severity; register/policy and target identity must be proven before injection.

original_test_intent: Inject an uncorrectable non-fatal PCIe error into every approved physical slot and prove the designated AER/WHEA non-fatal path, continued host operation and bounded endpoint/link recovery with platform-defined indicator behavior.
original_method: The FAE maps physical slot and endpoint/root-port BDF to a Cscript socket/port, confirms the selected error bit is unmasked and classified non-fatal, quiesces the endpoint, performs one UCE injection, then correlates AER/WHEA/register state with link/device recovery, optional management logs and physical indication before restoring settings.
manual_activity: The FAE approves physical/BDF mapping and non-fatal severity, quiesces the endpoint, changes BIOS controls, runs one UCE and owns any reset/recovery. The agent may validate register and health evidence.
required_inputs: PCIe slot to endpoint/root-port BDF and Cscript socket/port coverage
Endpoint identity/workload and independent management path
ITP/CScripts build/hash, exact injected AER bit and `uce` semantics
Severity/mask policy plus Windows WHEA/AER, link/device recovery and indicator oracle
Abort, OOB recovery and BIOS restoration plan
safety_requirements: Prove targeted bit is unmasked and non-fatal in current policy
One injection per freshly mapped slot with link/device monitoring
Abort on fatal escalation, host hang/reset, link loss, wrong target or persistent device failure
No retry; preserve evidence and restore settings/device health
agent_execution_scope: Validate mapping/severity captures and collect read-only Cscript, register, Windows, link/device, BMC/UEFI evidence
Do not select targets/severity, change BIOS, inject, reset/retry or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve slot coverage and non-fatal AER bit/policy
Define recovery and conditional log/indicator expectations

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic `uncorrected|non.fatal|MCE_` output does not prove the injected PCIe AER bit, target slot or recovery and conflicts with Windows.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use `errType='uce'` only after package documentation and current severity/mask registers show the resulting event is non-fatal for the mapped root port.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: PCIe slot 1~N, UCE stimulus, topology steps and 15/10-minute estimates are preserved; target and error-bit semantics are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Snapshot AER masks/severity, DPC policy, link speed/width and driver/device health; inject one mapped non-fatal bit; time-correlate WHEA/AER and any link recovery; confirm no host reset or permanent device loss; restore/diff state.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Turns the ambiguous `uce` token into a proven non-fatal AER event and measurable recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An uncorrected log cannot establish non-fatal classification or endpoint recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong severity or port may invoke DPC, reset a device, crash the host or affect storage/network/GPU service.

project_override_considerations: Because BMC/UEFI and the front-panel are all optional in the source, current AER/WHEA/register evidence plus continued host and endpoint health must be the mandatory acceptance core.
expected_evidence: Endpoint/workload precheck, package hash and exact AER bit
Pre/post severity/mask/DPC and full injection transcript
Windows WHEA/AER plus link/device/driver recovery and applicable BMC/UEFI/indicator evidence
Restoration, residual-error check and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Slot 1~N lacks a coverage map; `uce` does not define the injected AER bit or prove non-fatal severity; all BMC/UEFI/indicator outcomes are optional; Windows conflicts with dmesg; and DeepSeek's MCE grep is not a deterministic PCIe AER oracle.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The non-fatal PCIe UCE goal is identifiable and can be safely resolved with platform mapping, severity policy, package semantics and recovery inputs.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 32 Wistron-System RAS-00752-V003: approve PCIe slot-to-endpoint/root-port BDF and Cscript socket/port coverage, ITP/CScripts version/hash and exact `uce` AER bit; define current mask/severity/DPC policy proving non-fatal behavior, mandatory Windows WHEA/AER and link/device recovery when management logs/LED are optional, aborts, OOB recovery and restoration.

review_improvement: Requires proof that `uce` is actually non-fatal on the selected port and makes endpoint recovery—not an optional generic error log—the central result.
independent_technical_reasoning: PCIe uncorrectable is a class, not a severity guarantee. Whether an injected bit is non-fatal depends on AER severity/mask and DPC/firmware ownership for the current root port. The target chain and pre-state registers must therefore be captured before a single injection, and recovery must prove the endpoint and host remain usable. Since those mappings and policies can be supplied by the FAE, the case remains gated RPUC rather than BLOCKED.
